# v0.1.0

Second tagged release of goc, the self-contained C-subset compiler written in
pure Go. Same model as v0.0.1 — no libc, no external toolchain: goc lowers a
translation unit straight to a Windows PE32+ or Linux ELF64 via its own
assembler (goa), with the runtime (goclib) embedded as compilable C.

v0.1.0 is a correctness-and-capability milestone driven by running real-world
code (cJSON) through the compiler and fixing everything it exposed.

## Highlights

- **`main(int argc, char **argv)` now receives command-line arguments.**
  - Linux: the SysV entry stack already holds `argc`/`argv`; the stub captures
    them before realigning `rsp` and passes them in `rdi`/`rsi`.
  - Windows: a PE entry point gets neither, so goc links a small goclib helper
    (`__goclib_get_args`) that calls `GetCommandLineA` and tokenizes it
    (handling quotes, escaped quotes and backslashes) into `argv[0..]` with the
    program path as `argv[0]`.
- **Proper block-scoped local declarations.** A declaration is now resolved
  through a lexical scope stack instead of a single flat name table:
  - sibling blocks may reuse a name without their frame homes colliding;
  - an inner declaration shadows an outer one of the same name;
  - a `for (int i = …)` variable stays local to the loop;
  - nested blocks resolve to the correct enclosing variable.
  This removes the last reason for goclib's `i16/i32/i64/f32/f64` name-mangling
  workarounds.
- **cJSON compiles and runs under goc.** Used as a stress test, it surfaced
  and forced fixes for a string of compiler bugs (see below). cJSON is not
  bundled — it is a validation target.

## Bug fixes (found via cJSON + new regression examples)

- Integer literals parsed as 64-bit bit patterns (`ParseUint`), so
  `9223372036854775808` / `0x8000000000000000` no longer collapse to `0`.
- Lexer escape tables completed: `\b \f \a \v` (and the `\"` DB-operand case in
  goa) so escaped strings survive round-trips.
- `sizeof("string literal")` now yields the array size (was wrongly decaying to
  the pointer width).
- Pointer arithmetic expression typing: `p + 1`, `p - q`, and `(p + n)[i]` now
  carry the right type and element width, fixing a sign-flipped pointer
  difference and wrong index strides on `unsigned char *`.
- Array decay handled inside binary expressions and member/index lvalues, so
  `(a + 2)[0]` is a valid lvalue again.
- `cast` dereference read width follows the pointee, not the pointer (so
  `*(int *)p` reads 4 bytes, `*(double *)p` goes through `movsd`).

## Regression coverage

- New example `src/examples/scope.c` exercises sibling-block, shadowing,
  for-loop and nested-block scoping; it is executed on Windows and Linux across
  `-O0`/`-O1`/`-Os` in CI.
- Full pipeline regression: 295 checks green (Windows + Linux examples, goa
  assembler suite, three module unit-test suites).

## Assets

Identical layout to v0.0.1 — two versioned zips, plain names inside:

- `goc-<ver>-windows-x86_64.zip`: `goc.exe`, `cc.exe`, `goa.exe`,
  `README.md`, `LICENSE`
- `goc-<ver>-linux-x86_64.zip`: `goc`, `goa`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — checksums for both zips

`printf` width specifiers are still ignored (`%.Nf` precision on `%f`/`%g`
works); C99+ features (VLA, `_Generic`, file I/O / `math.h` beyond the bundled
subset) remain out of scope.
